days.label: 週一：詞彙語境與短篇閱讀

day_materials.title: Material: A School Garden Project
day_materials.content: A senior high school turned a small unused corner beside the gym into a garden. At first, only ten students joined the project because most classmates thought gardening was slow and messy. The teacher did not ask them to produce perfect vegetables. Instead, she asked each group to record sunlight, watering time, soil moisture, and changes in plant growth. After six weeks, the students noticed that the garden had become more than a science activity. Some used the herbs in cooking club, some wrote short poems about the plants, and others designed signs explaining how insects helped the garden. The project became popular because it connected science, language, art, and daily life.

question_slots.stem: In the sentence “The library started a quiet-hour policy to create a more ______ study environment,” which word best fits the blank?

day_materials.title: Material: A Repair Cafe
day_materials.content: A repair cafe is a community event where people bring broken items and learn how to fix them with volunteers. The goal is not only to save money, but also to reduce waste and rebuild trust among neighbors. When a lamp is repaired, the owner learns a skill; when a radio works again, a memory may return with it. These events remind people that objects do not always have to be thrown away, and that knowledge grows when it is shared.

day_materials.title: Material A: Tiny Libraries
day_materials.content: In several towns, residents have placed tiny book boxes on sidewalks. Anyone may take a book or leave one. The idea looks simple, but it changes how people think about public space. A box outside a bakery may attract children after school; another near a train station may serve commuters. Because no one checks membership cards, the system depends on trust. Some towns have found that the boxes also encourage conversations among strangers. A person who leaves a travel guide may later meet someone who used it for a weekend trip.

day_materials.title: Material B: Sleep and Study
day_materials.content: Many students believe that studying late into the night is a sign of effort. However, sleep researchers warn that memory does not work like a storage box that can be filled without rest. During sleep, the brain strengthens useful connections and clears away less important details. A short review before bed may help, but replacing sleep with extra hours of study often harms attention the next day. The question is not whether students should work hard, but whether their study plan gives the brain time to organize what it has learned.

question_slots.subject: 英文
question_slots.stem: According to the material, what is the main goal of Language Day?

options.text: To help students use English in real communication.
To test the hardest vocabulary in the textbook.
To replace all English classes.
To invite visitors to speak only Chinese.

question_slots.explanation: 材料說活動是讓學生在課本練習之外使用英文，重點是真實溝通。

question_slots.subject: 英文
question_slots.stem: Why do teachers ask students to focus on clear communication rather than difficult vocabulary?

options.text: Because difficult words are never useful.
Because successful communication depends on being understood.
Because students should avoid speaking English.
Because posters cannot include vocabulary.

question_slots.explanation: 清楚溝通比艱難單字更符合活動目的，B 是合理推論。
question_slots.review_advice: 推論題要從活動目的與老師提醒連結。
